question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{y+3}+2.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{y+3}+2,$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{\sqrt{y+3}-2} & = \\ \frac{5}{\sqrt{y+3}-2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{y+3}+2}{\sqrt{y+3}+2} & = \\ \frac{5(\sqrt{y+3}+2)}{(\sqrt{y+3}-2)(\sqrt{y+3}+2)} & = \\ \frac{5\sqrt{y+3}+10}{(\sqrt{y+3})^{2}-{2}^{2}} & = \\ \frac{5\sqrt{y+3}+10}{y+3-4} & = \\ \frac{5\sqrt{y+3}+10}{y-1}\end{aligned}
$$
